Hi, it's Owen Brandt. Quick question about moving money into savings.
Every time one of my outlets pays me, I move 25% of the deposit from checking to savings for taxes. I do it by hand in the app. Is there a way to have that happen automatically when a deposit posts?

Hi Owen, this is Member Services. We can't split a deposit by percentage, unfortunately. A recurring transfer has to be a set dollar amount, so the options are a fixed amount on a schedule or moving it yourself after each deposit posts.
Four outlets, and no two payments are ever the same size, so a fixed amount won't work. I'll stick with doing it by hand. Thanks for checking.

Hi Owen, this is the front desk at Riverview. The +1.25 readers you brought in for comparison on Tuesday got left behind in the exam room. We have them up front.
Ha, those are mine, and I haven't missed them once. The new +1.75s took over right away.
That's what we like to hear! If you don't need them back, we can put them in our donation box for used glasses.
Please donate them. And a belated 5 out of 5 for Tuesday.
Tires Plus: Reminder of your oil change tomorrow, Fri 9/18 at 8:00 AM, at our E Lake St store. Reply here with any questions, or call the store to reschedule.
Thanks, I'll be there. I'd rather wait than drop it off. Ok if I set up with a laptop in the waiting area while it's in?
Sure thing. There's a counter with outlets by the front window, and the Wi-Fi password is posted at the desk. A full synthetic change usually takes about 45 minutes.
Tires Plus: Your vehicle is ready. Total due $64.99. Thanks for your business.
Morning. Question about Friday's oil change. The new windshield sticker says next service in January, but the receipt says 5,000 miles or 6 months. Which should I go by?
Morning, Owen. Go by the sticker. The tech dated it early for winter, since short trips in the cold are harder on oil. The receipt just prints the standard interval.
That's most of our winter driving right there, short hops around town. January it is. Thanks.
Hi Owen, Northwoods Paddle Repair here. Your kayak is on the rack under ticket 2241 and goes on the bench Wednesday morning. We'll email a quote before doing any work.
Sounds good. I'm hoping to have it back for a paddle Saturday morning, if that's doable.
Your boat is ready. New stainless cable and sleeve are in, and the skeg drops and retracts clean. Total is $68.50 as quoted, and we're open until 6 today.
Great, I'll come by around four.
Second day out on the new cable, Taylors Falls down to Osceola today. Skeg was perfect, but I could hear sand grinding in the box when I raised it at the landing. Best way to flush it out?
Glad it's holding up. Drop the skeg, run a hose into the slot from the top until the water runs clear, then work the slider a few times. Do that after sandy landings and the new sleeve will last.

I'd like to, but this fall is spoken for. Ask me again after the new year.
Deal. I'll bug you in January.
Not the January ask, I promise. Smaller one. We get to public records in a couple of weeks. Do you have a data practices request letter I could show the class?
Ideally one that actually got you records. Half of them think a request is an email that ends with pretty please.
Also sorry, I just looked at the clock. It's Saturday. Answer whenever you're up.
Up now, no harm done. I keep a template adapted from the SEJ sample letter, and I'll send it this weekend. Tell them one subject per request, and ask for the spreadsheet, not a PDF of it.
That's going on the whiteboard word for word. Thank you, Owen.
Owen, could you help me carry the window air conditioner down to the basement sometime this week? No rush.
Happy to. How about Tuesday after five? I can bring the dolly.
Tuesday is perfect. I'll have coffee on.
Ingrid found the tomatoes on our back step and already ate one over the sink. Thank you, Bev.
Owen, no need to answer till morning. Your side gate has been banging for a while. I think the latch let go.
Went out with the flashlight. The catch is hanging by one screw. Glad it wasn't someone poking around back there.
I hooked a bungee cord from my garage around it and the post. Quiet now.
I don't sleep past four these days anyway, so don't fuss. Come by for coffee when you're up and have a look.
Morning Owen. I can look at those back steps tomorrow around 2 if that still works for you.
Tomorrow at 2 works. The side gate is unlatched, so come around back.
Two treads and a stringer replaced. Give them a couple weeks to dry before you stain. Bill's in your mailbox.
Thanks, Leif. The steps feel solid, and I found the bill. What should I use on the new treads so they don't look patchy next to the old ones?
Whatever's on the old treads, if you know what it is. If not, a semi-transparent in a cedar tone hides the difference best.
It's a cedar semi-transparent. There's half a can in the garage. So two weeks, then stain?
Two weeks if it stays dry. Sprinkle some water on a new tread first. If it soaks right in, it's ready. Call me if anything squeaks.

Yep, that was the main culprit. It was bent a few mm, probably from a tip-over. Shifts clean across the whole cassette now.
That tracks. It fell over in the garage last month.
Did the saddle height stay put? I had the seatpost marked with tape.
Tape's still on the post and the saddle is back at your mark. Heads up, your chain reads about 0.5 on the checker. Fine for this season, but plan on a new one in the spring.
